name: Japanese nationalism
summary: Japanese nationalism, in its main doctrinal form, holds that Japan is a unique nation whose core is the kokutai (national polity): an unbroken, sacred imperial line descended from Amaterasu, to which subjects owe absolute loyalty and filial devotion. The 1937 Kokutai no Hongi rejects individualism, liberalism, democracy, separated powers, class struggle and revolution as foreign, while absorbing foreign learning under the national polity, and treats conquest and the army as the emperor's will. The postwar movement (Nippon Kaigi) keeps the imperial house, national history, tradition and patriotic education and wants a home-made constitution and real self-defence.
scope: The nation question as the kokutai doctrine states it: identity, sacred imperial continuity, sovereignty, tradition, loyalty, the family, expansion, and the means it accepts, based on the 1937 Kokutai no Hongi, the 1890 Rescript on Education, the Meiji Constitution as the Kokutai no Hongi explains it, Tanaka Chigaku, and, for the postwar strand, Nippon Kaigi's declared aims on the constitution, the imperial house, history, education and defence. It excludes the economic and welfare programme of governments and parties that carried it (for example the LDP's), and the radical-reform strand (Kita Ikki), whose own text could not be opened.

notes: The old audit leaned on the Wikipedia article and the party and government programme; this one rests on the Kokutai no Hongi read in full (Japanese) and Nippon Kaigi's own pages. The Kokutai no Hongi is the state's statement for 1937 and Nippon Kaigi is postwar and does not claim the emperor's divinity or expansion, so answers on divinity, expansion and direct rule rest on the former only. Searched by theme: government, liberty, society, economy (national-duty framing only), world, culture, means. Economy, ecology, technology and most policy statements are null: no stated position. Not opened: the English Kokutai no Hongi (archive.org lending copy, 401), Kita Ikki's Outline Plan, Aizawa Seishisai's Shinron, the Rescript to Soldiers and Sailors, Britannica (bot wall). Tanaka's text is OCR with errors. Strand and scope pass (2026-10-30): answers resting on the Kokutai no Hongi alone were kept only with a second source (Rescript, Meiji Constitution and oath, Tanaka or Nippon Kaigi); where the prewar and postwar strands differ (divinity, divine authority, democracy, consent, constituent assembly, expansion, defensive-only wars, cultural equality, national mission) the answer is a split (0, low). Prewar general political theory (workers' councils, private courts, state as business, harm principle, self-ownership, self-interest, smash-the-state, withdrawal from politics, reason over faith, dictatorship of the proletariat, state as class instrument, material conditions, moral incentives, capitalism-communism, class collaboration, defeating communism, religion as illusion, night-watchman state, unjust law, personal loyalty rule) and positions only Nippon Kaigi states (collective defence, alliances, China, foreign suffrage, gender-as-construct) are null as no shared position. All 490 statements were checked. Review (2026-10-30): clerical-rule nulled (deduced, not stated).
